answer: Each identity binds a unique onyx core that thickens only via sequential timber rings from personal work. Influence scales with the density of the vine of interlocking proofs linking those rings—each new ring hashes the prior personal timber state plus fresh non-parallelizable computation. Attackers spinning clones pay the full sequential depth cost per head, since vine growth is strictly serial per onyx and rings cannot be shared; long-running agents accumulate density cheaply over time while farms cannot bootstrap high-weight identities without years of continuous per-identity compute.
